BugsWorld (prototype)
=====================

A browser-based replacement for the BugsWorld lab. Students upload the .bl
file they wrote and see compile errors right away, with line numbers and
hints, then submit. You run everyone's programs together in one simulation
and show it on the projector. Students install nothing.


1. Java 21 or newer
-------------------
To check, open a terminal (Command Prompt on Windows) and type:  java -version
If Java is missing or older than 21, install the free Temurin build from
https://adoptium.net. BugsWorld also tells you if your Java is too old.


2. Start BugsWorld
------------------
Windows:  double-click  "Start BugsWorld (Windows).bat"
Mac:      double-click  "Start BugsWorld (Mac).command"
          The first time, macOS may refuse to open a downloaded file:
          right-click it, choose Open, then choose Open again.
Linux:    run  bin/bugsworld

A window shows the server's messages; keep it open while you use BugsWorld.
Your browser opens the professor dashboard, already signed in. If it
doesn't, the window shows the link to open.
If your firewall asks whether Java may accept network connections, allow
it. Students' computers need to reach yours.


3. Try it on your own (about 2 minutes)
---------------------------------------
- On the dashboard, click "Add example programs to try it out".
- Click "Load everyone's newest program", then "Open projector view",
  then Start. Space pauses, the right arrow key steps one tick.
- To see what students see, open http://localhost:7070 in another tab
  and upload a file from the "examples" folder. Change a keyword or a
  name in one first to see the error messages.


4. In class
-----------
Students open the address shown at the top of the dashboard (something
like 192.168.1.20:7070) from a computer on the same network as yours.
They can only upload and submit. The simulation is visible only on your
dashboard and projector view, which need your instructor token.

Some campus Wi-Fi networks block computers from reaching each other. A
quick check in the classroom: open that address from your phone on the
same Wi-Fi. If the upload page appears, students will reach it too.


To stop BugsWorld, close its window (or press Ctrl+C in it). Submissions
and results are kept in the "BugsWorld" folder in your home folder.
